setupSteps: Space and floor. Clear about a 1 m × 1 m patch of flat, non-slip floor. Bare feet or a sticky mat on a hard floor; never socks on tiles or a thick, squishy mat that makes balance harder.
Wall. Stand about one arm's length from a wall or beside a sturdy chair or countertop. A beginner can start with the back or the side of the body near the wall.
Clothing. Wear clothes that let the knee bend and the hip open (shorts, leggings, loose pants rolled up). Avoid a long kurta or dupatta that can get under the standing foot.
Stance start. Stand tall with feet together or about 5 cm apart (the AYUSH protocol text, as seen in snippets, mentioned about two inches apart), weight even on both feet.
Pick a drishti (gaze point). Choose a still point at eye level on the wall, such as a mark or a picture frame, before lifting anything.
Camera. Phone on a shelf at hip height, 2 to 2.5 m in front (see sections 11 and 12).

steps.title: Stand tall in Mountain pose
steps.action: feet together, arms by the sides, shoulders down, crown of the head lifted.
steps.feel: weight even through both feet, light core engagement.
steps.breathing: 2 slow breaths in and out through the nose.
steps.visualCheck: front view, head, shoulders and hips level; side view, ear over shoulder over hip over ankle.

steps.title: Fix your gaze
steps.action: look at the chosen point at eye level and keep looking.
steps.feel: the head settles and the eyes soften.
steps.tempo: stay on the point for the whole pose.
steps.visualCheck: chin level, not dropped toward the floor.

steps.title: Shift weight to the standing foot
steps.action: slowly move weight onto the left foot, pressing through the big toe, little toe and heel.
steps.feel: the standing leg wakes up; the other foot gets light.
steps.visualCheck: front view, hips stay level; the standing hip does not push out sideways.

steps.title: Soften the standing knee
steps.action: keep the left leg straight but with the knee soft, never locked back.
steps.feel: thigh engaged, no strain behind the knee.
steps.visualCheck: side view, knee straight but not pushed back.

steps.title: Lift the right foot, bending the knee
steps.action: bend the right knee and lift the foot off the floor, with the knee turning out to the side.
steps.feel: a gentle opening in the right hip.
steps.visualCheck: front view, the raised knee points out to the side, hips still level.

steps.title: Place the foot (choose one height)
steps.action: set the sole of the right foot against the left leg. Beginner: toes on the floor with the heel at the left ankle ("kickstand"), or the foot on the inner ankle. Next level: the inner calf, below the knee. Advanced: the inner thigh, above the knee. Press the foot and the leg gently into each other. Never press the foot into the knee.
steps.feel: steady pressure between foot and leg; no pinch at the knee.
steps.visualCheck: front view, the foot sits clearly below or above the standing knee, not on it.

steps.title: Square the hips
steps.action: draw both hip points forward, like two headlights shining ahead, so the pelvis does not twist.
steps.feel: even weight, lower belly gently drawn in.
steps.visualCheck: front view, hip line level; the raised-side hip is not jutting out.

steps.title: Bring the hands to the chest
steps.action: palms together in front of the chest (Anjali mudra), thumbs resting on the breastbone.
steps.visualCheck: front view, elbows out, shoulders not shrugged.

steps.title: Optional: raise the arms
steps.action: only if you are comfortable and have no high blood pressure concern, slowly raise the arms overhead, palms together or shoulder-width apart.
steps.feel: a lift through the sides of the body; no strain in the neck.
steps.breathing: breathe in as the arms rise.
steps.visualCheck: front view, ribs not flared, shoulders away from the ears.

steps.title: Hold
steps.action: stay steady, eyes on the point, small wobbles are normal.
steps.feel: ankle and hip making tiny corrections.
steps.breathing: slow nose breaths, do not hold your breath.
steps.tempo: 20 to 30 seconds (about 5 to 8 breaths; chosen). Sources give breaths, not seconds: 5 to 8 and 5 to 10 breaths were seen.
steps.visualCheck: standing knee soft, hips level, head tall.

steps.title: Release
steps.action: lower the arms, then lower the raised foot slowly back to the floor, returning to Mountain pose.
steps.feel: a shake-out of the legs; warmth.

steps.title: Repeat on the other side. Do the same hold on the right leg. Use the same height of foot placement on each side, or go lower on the harder side

commonMistakes.title: Foot on the knee joint
commonMistakes.text: Foot on the knee joint. A foot pressed into the side of the standing knee can strain the joint sideways. Fix: move the foot below the knee (calf or ankle) or above it (inner thigh).

commonMistakes.title: Looking down or around
commonMistakes.text: Looking down or around. The eyes drifting causes the head to drop and balance to go. Fix: choose an eye-level point before lifting the foot and keep it.

commonMistakes.title: Hip jutting out to the side
commonMistakes.text: Hip jutting out to the side. The raised-side hip pops up and the torso twists, so balance is lost and the standing hip is over-loaded. Fix: draw both hip points forward and keep the hips level.

commonMistakes.title: Locking the standing knee back
commonMistakes.text: Locking the standing knee back. It can strain the back of the knee and makes sway worse. Fix: keep a soft bend and engage the thigh.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. It raises tension and makes wobbles worse. Fix: breathe slowly through the nose.

commonMistakes.title: Rushing up to the thigh
commonMistakes.text: Rushing up to the thigh. Too-high placement with a stiff hip makes the pelvis tilt or the knee torque. Fix: start with toes on the floor or the ankle and move up only when steady.

commonMistakes.title: Gripping the foot or leg too hard with the toes
commonMistakes.text: Gripping the foot or leg too hard with the toes. It tires the foot and adds tension. Fix: press with the whole sole, keep the toes loose.

commonMistakes.title: Arms overhead with high blood pressure or neck tension
commonMistakes.text: Arms overhead with high blood pressure or neck tension. Some teaching sources advise keeping hands at the chest if you have high blood pressure. Fix: Anjali mudra at the chest.

commonMistakes.title: Practising on a slippery or soft surface, or in socks
commonMistakes.text: Practising on a slippery or soft surface, or in socks. Higher risk of slipping. Fix: bare feet on a flat, non-slip floor; wall nearby.

safetyNotes: Foot placement: never on the knee joint. Use ankle, calf or inner thigh. Skip if placing the foot hurts the hip or knee.
Balance and falls: always start near a wall or sturdy support; the pose is a balance challenge, so use support if you wobble repeatedly.

Dizziness, vertigo, low or high blood pressure: sources listed vertigo and low blood pressure (when held too long) as cautions; one source also listed headache and insomnia as cautions. Skip arms overhead with high blood pressure.
Recent injury or surgery: one source advised against the pose for ankle or knee injuries less than 3 months old; others list hip, knee and shoulder injuries as reasons to modify. Ask a doctor.

Pregnancy: prenatal yoga sources advise a wall or chair nearby because balance can be affected by shifting centre of gravity; one prenatal page said to avoid the pose with symphysis pubis dysfunction (SPD). An ACOG statement on tree pose was Not found.
Stop immediately if you feel: sudden dizziness, sharp pain in the knee, hip or ankle, a twisting or popping feeling in the knee, chest pain, shortness of breath or a feeling of fainting.
Spotter: not needed; use a wall or chair as support.
Gym etiquette: use a clear spot in the stretching area, away from walkways and free weights.

Foot height: ankle (beginner), calf, inner thigh (advanced); the knee joint is avoided. We start beginners at the ankle or kickstand.
Arms: chest or overhead; we default to the chest and advise it for high blood pressure.
